key_insight: The paper observes that robots learn task steps and object roles—not visual appearance—from in-context examples. This suggests a route to transferring manipulation experience across scenes, although the provided abstract is incomplete.
problem_solved: Trained manipulation policies are tied to their training distributions, while in-context approaches struggle because demonstrations from other scenes lack feedback from the robot’s current environment.
method: Use in-context experience to guide manipulation rather than encoding every skill through policy training.
Represent experience through semantic task steps and object roles instead of scene-specific appearance.
Motivate connecting contextual experience with current-world feedback; the truncated abstract does not specify the mechanism.
impact: For robotics practitioners, this points toward reusing manipulation knowledge across changing environments with less reliance on retraining. Performance gains and implementation details cannot be established from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: skills stored in network weights versus task knowledge supplied in context.
Two visually different scenes annotated with matching object roles and task steps.
Feedback-loop illustration linking contextual experience, robot actions, and the current environment.
Semantic task sequence showing how object roles remain stable despite changes in appearance.
paper_title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang, Mingyang Du, Dingkang Liang
